caption: LUM-1312 chat-input parity: a multi-line draft with codex-style editing. Ctrl+J (Shift+Enter on kitty-protocol terminals) opens a new line instead of submitting; Up/Down move by visual row and keep the display column; Ctrl+A/Ctrl+E are scoped to the current line; Ctrl+U/Ctrl+K kill to the line edges; the prompt history is reached from the top row; a trailing backslash + Enter inserts a newline in a terminal that cannot report Shift+Enter at all. Every frame is a real PTY at 76x26 driving the debug binary built from this commit.

panels.label: 1. idle: one composer row, `? for help` in the header
2. Ctrl+J inserts a newline: the composer grows to two rows and does NOT submit

probe.why: the first line keeps the label
the second line is a real draft row, indented like a wrapped continuation row
the cursor sits at the end of the new line

panels.label: 3. Up moves one visual row and keeps the display column (14 columns here, the width of the second line)

probe.why: Up left the second row, so no `and add a test▍`; the caret is on the first row, 14 columns in — the sticky column codex and pi both implement

panels.label: 4. Down comes back to the row it left

probe.why: Down returns to the second row

panels.label: 5. Ctrl+A is scoped to the current line: line 2's start, line 1 untouched. (Bare Home is the chat-log jump, as upstream binds it: `tui.altScreen.top`.)

probe.why: the caret is at the start of line 2, not at the start of the draft

panels.label: 6. Ctrl+U kills to the start of the current line only

probe.why: the first line survives — Ctrl+U is line-scoped, not a buffer clear

panels.label: 7. Ctrl+Y yanks the killed line back at the cursor

probe.why: the kill ring round-trips the line: the restored text sits at the cursor, which is at the start of line 2

panels.label: 8. Enter submits the two-line draft as one prompt

probe.why: the submitted prompt is echoed in the transcript

panels.label: 9. Up on the empty composer recalls the two-line prompt from the history

probe.why: the recall restores the whole multi-line draft...

panels.label: 10. a 95-character draft on line 2 wraps across three composer rows at 76 columns

probe.why: characters past the body width (74 columns) continue on an indented row: character 74 is the 5th of the repeating 0-9 run

panels.label: 11. Up inside the wrapped draft moves the caret one row up, keeping the label row intact

probe.why: the caret is still drawn somewhere in the composer
the labelled row is unchanged by the move

panels.label: 12. /help advertises the chords that reach the editor in the real app

probe.why: Ctrl+J is advertised as the newline chord, because it is the one every terminal can deliver

probe.text: delete to the end of the line
probe.why: the line-scoped kills are advertised instead of the old buffer clear
